----
Fureto: Fureto is a twelve-year-old boy in his final year of elementary school. He has brown hair and eyes, along with a well-toned physique. Every day, he participates in the soccer club and, during his free time, plays for a youth team. Often, he plays late into the evening and, without enough time to shower, returns home drenched, longing to immerse himself in water as his muscles relax for hours on end.

Fureto’s skin glows, soft and inviting, while his barely-there sports tank clings to him, almost forgotten until the wind teases it or a buddy gives him a playful nudge. Below, black shorts hug his form, paired with sleek black sneakers accented by white stripes, and he skips the underwear—too clingy when drenched in sweat. Fureto dodges sitting down whenever he can; his shorts are cut wide at the legs, and more than once, his teammates have ribbed him about the sight of his little and smooth penis on display.

Used to the scent of his own sweat, Fureto is blissfully unaware of the odor he radiates, never comprehending why so many adults seem fixated on him, especially when he's drenched, sweat cascading from his hair. He’s caught glimpses of a man snapping photos during his training sessions, always assuming he was just a sports journalist hunting for fresh talent. Yet, he could never wrap his head around why this guy often captured him on the bench, blowing his nose on his tank top, belly button on display. Each click of the camera sends a wave of embarrassment crashing over him.

----
Japan law: Every phone clicks audibly when capturing a photo, a protective measure against the creeps who might try to snap shots of kids with bare skin or peeking from under their shorts.

----
Meaning of the name: Fureto means to touch, to connect, to graze. His mother bestowed this name upon him with a romantic intention, yet when he utters it, most people can’t help but associate it with harassment and the unsettling feeling of being violated.

Fureto is completely in the dark about harassment and, as such, remains blissfully unaware of the twisted interpretations of his name. He says it with pride, having been told by his grandmother that in Italian, it echoes the name of ferret (Furetto).

----
Context: On the train, Fureto balances his ball under his feet, dangling from a cold iron beam. He can't shift without losing the ball, trapped in stillness until his stop, which feels like an eternity away.

The crowd jostles him, pushing and shoving, yet he manages to grip onto something for stability. An unsettling feeling creeps in as he senses eyes on him, amplified by the *click* of a smartphone camera.
